sections.h2: Wages are the largest income source for the average agricultural household

chart.title: Wages lead every other income source on the imputed-cost basis
chart.sub: Average monthly income per agricultural household, ₹, imputed-cost basis, 2018-19.

sections.means: On the imputed-cost basis, wages make up 49% of household income and crop production 37%.
sections.todo: Treat wage income as the main income line when sizing any farm-income policy built on this survey.

sections.h2: Wages beat crop income on both expense bases, by ₹265 to ₹1,005 a month

chart.title: The wage lead over crop income widens on the fuller expense basis
chart.sub: Wages minus net receipt from crop production, ₹ per month, 2018-19.

sections.means: Wages stay ahead of crop income on either basis, and the gap is wider once family labour is costed.
sections.todo: Report the wage lead on the imputed-cost basis, since that is the fuller measure of what the household earns.

sections.h2: Imputing family labour cost cuts animal income more than crop income

chart.title: Costing family labour removes more from animal income than from crop income
chart.sub: Drop in monthly income from paid-out to imputed-cost basis, ₹ per household, 2018-19.

sections.means: Animal income falls by ₹1,141 a month once family labour is costed, against ₹740 for crop production.
sections.todo: Check any livestock income figure against the imputed-cost basis before using it in policy.
